headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:3.9}} on the summit of Jay Peak Sunday night to Monday afternoon, and {{s:6.5}} for the week. None of the resorts close to opening get cold enough to make snow this week. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Showers will be widespread through early afternoon, and then more scattered towards evening when a rumble of thunder is possible.
Some additional showers are expected over the weekend as temperatures gradually return closer to normal.
Somewhat unsettled weather is expected for much of next week.

ALY.excerpt:
) A weak cold front will bring scattered showers to the region Thursday, with additional chances of rain Friday into Friday night for the I-84 corridor in NY and Litchfield County in CT.
) Another disturbance will lead to a round of scattered showers across the region Saturday into early Sunday, with temperatures trending back towards normal Sunday into early next week.

GYX.excerpt: A wetter period begins today with scattered showers moving in ahead of a frontal boundary. A soaking rain is likely Friday and Saturday at the coast as the front stalls offshore, with beneficial rain inland as well.

BUF.excerpt:
) Showers to pass east across the region early this morning, then breezy conditions today.
) Unsettled weather and cooler temperatures Friday through the weekend.

PHI.excerpt: A slow moving cold front approaches and moves through the area on Friday, bringing the potential for heavy rain to portions of the area beginning on Thursday.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild through Friday with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell now over.
) Trending cooler this weekend with lake enhanced rain showers beneath upper level low

RLX.excerpt:
) Showers taper off today as a cold front moves through.
) Much cooler temperatures arrive this weekend behind the cold front, setting up frost/freeze concerns across our active growing season counties.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Some snow Sunday evening, best at Smugglers' Notch.
paras: The main event runs Sunday evening to Monday afternoon. Smugglers' Notch {{s:4}}, Stowe {{s:4}}, Jay Peak {{s:3.9}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.1,5.7}} at Smugglers' Notch. It's a northwest upslope setup, one that usually favors Smugglers' Notch, Stowe and Jay Peak. Rain mixes in at the bases. Confidence is low so far (1% odds of {{s:6}}+), so expect changes.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:39}} to {{t:57}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
Trend: totals have gone up since yesterday, led by Jay Peak ({{s:1}} to {{s:5.4}}).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Thursday 6:18 AM: "Showers will be widespread through early afternoon, and then more scattered towards evening when a rumble of thunder is possible."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

insights.text: Accumulating snow: about {{s:3.9}} at the summit Sunday night to Monday afternoon (models {{r:0,4.7}}). The base ({{e:1800}}) mixes with or changes to rain early Monday: about {{s:0.1}} there vs {{s:3.9}} up top. Highs stay near {{t:35}} afterward, so some of it should stick up high.
Too mild to make snow this week: mid-mountain doesn't stay at or below {{t:26}} (counting humidity) for long.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 22 days out.
